properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 700 PM EST.

* At 602 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 26 nm southeast of Carysfort Reef Light,
moving northwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 2:30PM PST until November 18 at 5:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area...

* Until 530 PM PST.

* At 230 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Timber Burn Area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within
Lafler, Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between
Grimes and Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Highway 1 near mile marker 50 south of
Andrew Molera State Park to mile maker 38. Other areas impacted
include Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park Campground and Partington Ridge,
structures along the Big Sur River, Mule Creek Canyon, and adjacent
drainages and watershed outlets.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin

* WHEN...Until 445 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1253 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 9:10 AM
Wed 11/18, 1.3 ft above normal (6.2 ft MLLW) at 9:41 AM Thu
11/19, 1.6 ft above normal (6.5 ft MLLW) at 10:07 AM Fri
11/20, and 2.0 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 10:32 AM Sat
11/21.
* West Sacramento: 1.4 ft above normal (5.7 ft MLLW) at 12:09
PM Wed 11/18, 1.6 ft above normal (6.0 ft MLLW) at 12:37 PM
Thu 11/19, 1.9 ft above normal (6.3 ft MLLW) at 1:04 PM Fri
11/20, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 1:35 PM Sat
11/21.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +6.5 ft at 11:00 AM Wed 11/18,
+6.9 ft at 12:00 PM Thu 11/19, +6.4 ft at 12:00 PM Fri 11/20,
and +6.8 ft at 1:00 PM Sat 11/21.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:21AM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
